title: instrument-prefetch-shard-latency-and-add-synthetic-token-trace-generator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent latency spikes originating from the prefetch path in the serving runtime. On investigation, spikes correlate to a small number of heavy shards where prefetch work queues pile up and cause backpressure across concurrent requests. Existing telemetry exposed only request-level prefetch timings; we lacked shard-level visibility and a reliable way to reproduce the long-tail behavior in CI. This PR adds shard-scoped prefetch metrics, a synthetic token-trace generator to reproduce prefetched-KV patterns, an observability dashboard to surface shard hotspots, and tuned alerts that reduce false positives from noisy tenants.

What this PR changes (summary):
- Instrumentation: add per-shard prefetch metrics (prefetch_latency_ms_histogram, prefetch_queue_depth_gauge, prefetched_tokens_count) with stable labels: tenant_id, route, model_name, shard_id, and prefetch_reason. Metrics are emitted from the prefetch worker and at request-join points to correlate request latency with outstanding prefetch work.
- Synthetic trace generator: introduce telemetry/traces/synthetic_generator.py, a small harness that emits OpenTelemetry spans representing token-level generation with configurable prefix lengths, KV prefetch delays, and per-token compute latencies. The generator can be run in CI/canary clusters to inject controlled workloads and validate sampling, aggregation, and alerting behavior.
- Dashboards: add a new prefetch-shard heatmap dashboard (observability/dashboards/prefetch-shard-heatmap.json). Panels include: shard p95/p99 latency heatmap, queue-depth time-series, request-to-prefetch waterfall, and a drilldown for top-N noisy shards by tenant.
- Alerts: introduce per-shard adaptive alerting rule (observability/alerts/prefetch-shard-alerts.yaml). Alerts use a two-stage detector: (1) p95/p99 surge detector with short window for immediate action, (2) per-shard noise suppression using decaying suppression windows to avoid chasing noisy tenants. Alerts surface shard_id and tenant_id for quick triage and include runbook links.
- Tests and examples: add unit tests for metrics emission and an example HCL job that runs the synthetic generator against a canary telemetry endpoint (examples/telemetry/prefetch-replay.hcl). Also add docs describing how to run the generator and interpret the dashboard (docs/observability/prefetch-tracing.md).

Why this implementation: Shard-level metrics let us isolate that a small subset of shards cause disproportionate delay. The synthetic generator provides deterministic replay for CI and debugging without requiring production traffic. The alert tuning reduces noisy alert fatigue while preserving signal for genuine regressions.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Metrics use new metric names with stable labels and are gated behind an opt-in runtime flag (ENABLE_PREFETCH_SHARD_METRICS) to allow gradual rollout.
- Synthetic trace generator is behind a telemetry feature flag and can be deployed only to canary clusters initially.
- Dashboard and alerts are added to the default observability repo but alerts are disabled by default; they are promoted to enabled during the canary monitoring phase after two days of stable signals.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for metrics emission and label cardinality checks (serving/prefetch/prefetch_test.go).
- Integration run on staging canary: synthetic generator replayed 10k synthetic invocations over 6 hours to validate histogram buckets and alert thresholds.
- CI: lint, unit, and telemetry e2e run passed in canary environment.

Release notes: "Adds shard-level prefetch telemetry, a synthetic token trace generator for replaying prefetch-heavy workloads, a new dashboard to surface shard hotspots, and tuned per-shard alerts to reduce noisy paging."

Maya Chen: Added tenant label whitelist and cardinality test in the latest commit; the test asserts <= 50 distinct tenant labels for test fixture. See serving/prefetch/prefetch_test.go:TestLabelCardinality.
Laura Kim: Dashboard looks good, but can we add a panel that normalizes by requests/sec to see per-request prefetch cost?
Maya Chen: Added per-request normalized chart and a small explainer in the dashboard JSON; it helped reveal a tenant with high prefetch tokens per request.
Diego Morales: Alert suppression logic seems sensible; add ACLs for runbook links so on-call can acknowledge and mute a shard without a full page.
Maya Chen: Runbook link now resolves to the internal playbook and the alert includes a 'mute-shard' quick-action link wired to the SRE tool.
Laura Kim: CI failed once on telemetry e2e due to timing assumptions; re-ran the job and it passed. Approving now.
Arjun Patel: LGTM, approving and squashing commits for merge.

release_notes: Add shard-level prefetch telemetry and synthetic token trace generator. New dashboard to identify shard hotspots. Per-shard adaptive alerts with noise suppression. Feature gated behind ENABLE_PREFETCH_SHARD_METRICS.
notes_for_ops: When enabling the metric flag: monitor metric cardinality for first 48 hours. If shard label cardinality grows unexpectedly, flip the feature off and contact the author. Alerts are disabled by default; enable them after verifying the heatmap on canary for 48 hours.
